title: Sell Mineral Rights in Riverview, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Riverview, AL | Escambia County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Riverview, AL along the Escambia County river system? Get an honest, title-checked offer, no pressure to sign anything.
heroLead: Riverview sits along Escambia County's river bottomland, close enough to the deep gas exploration around Vocation Field to have seen occasional leasing interest, even where drilling itself never followed.
intro: A lot of families near Riverview hold mineral interests that were leased once, decades ago, when exploration activity swept through this part of Escambia County chasing the deep Norphlet trend, but no well was ever actually drilled on their specific tract. That distinction matters — a leased-but-undrilled interest is a genuinely different situation from a producing one, and pricing it honestly starts with knowing which category applies.

sections.heading: Leased but Never Drilled
paragraphs: If your family signed a lease near Riverview but no well was ever put on the property, that lease may have expired on its own after the primary term, returning full ownership to your family without anyone formally telling you. We check the lease's current status before saying anything about what your interest is worth today.

sections.heading: River-Bottom Terrain and What It Means for Access
paragraphs: Like other river-bottom communities in south Alabama, Riverview's terrain has shaped how operators approach drilling here, with easier-access upland tracts generally seeing more activity than low-lying river-bottom acreage. We factor that reality into how we look at your specific tract rather than pricing it the same as easily accessible ground.

faqs.question: We signed a lease years ago but no well was ever drilled. Do we still own the minerals?
faqs.answer: In most cases, yes — an expired lease with no production simply returns the mineral rights to the owner. We confirm that against the courthouse record.

faqs.question: Does being on river-bottom land near Riverview limit our options?
faqs.answer: It can affect how operators have historically approached leasing, which factors into value, but it doesn't limit your ability to sell what you own.

faqs.question: How do we find out if a lease on our land is still active?
faqs.answer: Send us the lease if you have it, or the legal description, and we'll check the current status at the Escambia County Courthouse.

faqs.question: Is our family's interest worth more if we wait to see if drilling ever happens nearby?
faqs.answer: That's a real tradeoff, and it depends on your family's timeline and risk tolerance. We can walk through both the current offer and how nearby activity might affect it.

faqs.question: What paperwork should we pull together before reaching out?
faqs.answer: An old deed or lease is helpful, but not required. Even a rough legal description or family name is enough for us to start the courthouse search.
